topic.title: Structured Prediction and Differentiable Inference
topic.overview: Structured prediction learns outputs such as alignments, matchings, or parse trees whose components must satisfy joint constraints. These papers connect parameter learning with the optimization used to decode a valid structure. Large-margin objectives, convex relaxations, and differentiable dynamic programs offer different ways to make inference part of training.
topic.whyItMatters: An accurate approximation to an inference score can still mislead a learning algorithm or make good predictions unreachable. Guarantees must therefore cover the combination of training objective and inference procedure, not only each component in isolation.
topic.evolution: The collection spans early learning from structured objects and max-margin models. The 2000s representatives examine compatible approximate inference and dual losses. More recent work studies certified generalization and learnable dynamic-program parameters, including efficient second-order derivatives needed to train alignment and parsing marginals end to end.
openQuestions: Which relaxations preserve the predictions that matter after discretization?
How can learned inference parameters retain meaningful constraints outside the training distribution?
